summary:
Project Bio Orbit is an intelligent health monitoring software designed to safeguard astronauts during space missions. Addressing the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge, our platform continuously tracks, analyzes, and visualizes astronauts' vital signs—such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep patterns, and stress levels—in real time.
Space environments expose crews to microgravity, radiation, and isolation, which can rapidly impact human physiology. Bio Orbit bridges the communication gap between space crews and mission control by detecting early anomalies, predicting potential health risks, and providing actionable medical insights before emergencies occur. Built using open-source NASA human research and biomedical datasets, the software ensures crew autonomy during deep-space missions where real-time Earth communication is delayed. Ultimately, Project Bio Orbit enhances crew safety, optimizes mission performance, and paves the way for sustainable long-duration human space exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Project Bio Orbit is a comprehensive, real-time health monitoring software designed specifically for astronauts on deep-space and orbital missions. The platform continuously collects, analyzes, and visualizes critical physiological metrics—including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), body temperature, sleep cycles, and stress indicators. Using intelligent anomaly detection, Bio Orbit compares live biometric telemetry against each astronaut's personalized baseline profile. When irregularities occur, the system triggers instant alerts and provides step-by-step onboard medical guidance, enabling crews to respond effectively even during Earth communication blackouts.
Benefits
  • Proactive Health Management:Detects subtle physiological changes early before they escalate into life-threatening medical emergencies.
  • Crew Autonomy: Empowers astronauts to monitor their own health and follow guided interventions without waiting for delayed instructions from Mission Control.
  • Reduced Cognitive Load: Presents complex biomedical data in a clean, glanceable dashboard so astronauts can focus on critical mission tasks.
Intended Impact
As human spaceflight expands toward long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. Project Bio Orbit bridges this gap by establishing an autonomous, reliable onboard health assistant. Beyond space exploration, this technology can be adapted for remote environments on Earth—such as polar research stations, submarines, and rural clinics—where immediate access to specialist doctors is limited.
Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used
  • Development Platform: Built and prototyped using Google AI Studio, leveraging modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/TypeScript) for a responsive, low-latency interface.
  • Data & Analytics: Structured around open-source physiological parameters and health benchmarks inspired by NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) and Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).
  • AI Integration: Utilized Super Intelligence (SI) tools to assist in code generation, UI/UX structuring, and simulating astronaut biometric scenarios.
Creativity
Unlike standard terrestrial fitness trackers that only log historical data, Bio Orbit is engineered as a mission-critical "co-pilot" for human physiology in space. Its adaptive alert system dynamically adjusts thresholds based on mission phases (such as launch, extravehicular activities/spacewalks, and rest periods), combining predictive health insights with actionable emergency protocols in a single unified interface.
Key Factors Considered by Our Team
  • Space Physiology: Accounted for microgravity-induced fluid shifts, cardiovascular deconditioning, radiation exposure risks, and circadian rhythm disruptions.
  • Communication Latency: Designed an offline-first architecture that operates independently without requiring a constant connection to Earth.
  • Human Factors & UX: Prioritized high-contrast, clutter-free visual design to ensure rapid readability and zero confusion under high-stress, zero-gravity conditions.
